claims.text: The proposed computational framework combines Cluster Expansion, the Quasi-Harmonic Approximation, and a machine-learned correction term.
The hybrid framework will predict melting temperature, entropy of fusion, and heat capacity of RHEAs within 5% error.
The hybrid framework will outperform standard CALPHAD extrapolations in both speed and accuracy for multicomponent systems.
The hybrid framework will outperform pure DFT calculations in both speed and accuracy for multicomponent systems.
W20Mo20Ta20Nb20V20 is an example of a refractory high-entropy alloy.
The target RHEAs initially form disordered BCC solid solutions.
Experimental melting data for the target alloys are sparse or unreliable because their melting temperatures exceed 2000 K.
The applicable high-entropy composition regime contains at least five principal elements in near-equimolar proportions, including refractory elements such as W, Mo, Ta, Nb, and V.
A Cluster Expansion parameterized with DFT calculations of ordered binary and ternary supercells can represent the configurational energy landscape.
The Quasi-Harmonic Approximation can calculate the alloys' vibrational free-energy contributions up to the melting point.
An ML model trained on DFT-QHA residuals can account for anharmonic and magnetic contributions omitted by standard QHA.
Anharmonic phonon-phonon interactions and severe lattice distortion become significant near melting in multicomponent refractory alloys.
Standard CALPHAD models struggle because binary and ternary extrapolations fail to capture nonlinear effects such as severe lattice distortion and local chemical ordering in HEAs.
Pure DFT is too computationally expensive to sample the configurational space required for accurate melting-point prediction through thermodynamic integration.
The hybrid model will achieve a melting-temperature MAE below 50 K on novel RHEA compositions.
Standard CALPHAD extrapolations will have melting-temperature errors above 150 K.
Pure DFT methods will be computationally infeasible for screening more than 1000 compositions.
Entropy of fusion decreases as atomic-size mismatch increases because of lattice distortion.
The method is valid only for substitutional RHEAs that remain BCC up to melting.
The method is not applicable when phase separation, dominant intermetallic or B2 formation, or inadequately represented magnetic transitions control the thermodynamics.

contradictions.description: The claimed target is within 5% error and specifically below 50 K MAE, but falsification requires error above 10% or 150 K. Results between 5% and 10%, or between 50 K and 150 K, would violate the stated performance claim without satisfying the falsification rule.
